sources.note: Listed by Kinnaird 2006 among 'previous studies with some reference to Vamé/Pelasla'; comparative treatment of Central Chadic vowel/prosody systems that occasionally notes accent

sources.note: The Phonology page contains only 'Coming soon.'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William & Annukka Kinnaird (comp.). 2023. Dictionnaire Vamé. Webonary.org, SIL. Overview > Introduction and Language > Phonology pages (phonology page currently 'Coming soon')
sources.note: Dictionary front matter may eventually carry the phonology summary from the 2010 sketch; the Introduction page could not be read (an automated-access block) and the Phonology page is empty as of 2026-09-17.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.note: Explicitly excludes tone and stress from the reconstruction ('though not including tone or stress'). §5.3.6 Hurza group (pp.122-125) summarises Vame segmental/prosodic phonology from A. Kinnaird 2010: palatalization prosody only (no labialization prosody), two underlying vowels /a ə/, labialized velars, palatalized laminals. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William J. 2006. The Vamé verbal system. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministère de la Recherche Scientifique et de l'Innovation. 66 pp. (SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 47829)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. §1.3.2 gives the vowel/consonant inventories; §2.4 'Verb tone' (p.12) says tone has an important grammatical function in the verb, verb roots divide into basically-Low and basically-High classes, and conjugated verbs undergo 'tonal fluctuation' while other word classes keep fixed tone patterns (p.8). Full-text scanned search for stress/accent/prominence: no hits (only 'high tone on syllable preceding the affix', p.~47, a tonal statement).

sources.citation: Kinnaird, William. 2005. Proposition d'orthographe pour la langue vamé. Yaoundé: SIL. 22 pp. (SIL archive entry 47830; in French)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent tonique. §2.3.1 'Le ton' (p.7): a few tonal minimal pairs exist among nouns but tone is written only on verbal pronouns and some functors; §3.2 (p.11): 'Il n'y a pas beaucoup de mots en vamé qui se différencient uniquement par leurs tons.. Dans la flexion verbale, par contre, le ton joue un rôle important'. The word 'accents' there refers to orthographic diacritics marking grammatical function, not stress.

sources.citation: Grant, Caroline A. 1992. A sociolinguistic survey of Pəlasla (rapid appraisal). Yaoundé: SIL. 17 pp. (SIL archive entry 47831)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic survey. Only speakers' remarks that the Hurza/Dumwa varieties differ 'in tone'.

sources.note: A manuscript on verbal information structure/morphology of Ouldémé and Vamé; since Kinnaird 2006 §2.4 treats Vamé verb tone as grammatical (Low- vs High-toned root classes, tonal marking of TAM on pronoun clitics), this earlier verb study may contain verb-tone observations, but its contents are unseen.
